summary: A 30-foot steel fire lookout on Tower Mountain in the Prescott National Forest, first used in 1911 and registered in 2003; the register lists it in active service.

facts.design: 30-foot D-2 style Pacific Coast Steel tower with a modified L-4 cab

staffing.status: In active service per the 2003 register; no current staffing found

access.note: Described as in active Forest Service service; no source says the cab is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: A trail guide describes a forest road from Crown King to the lookout area and says almost any high-clearance vehicle can make the trip when there is no snow. Ask the Bradshaw Ranger District before visiting.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the present tower to 1933, but a 1924 newspaper reported a tower already completed on the mountain. A September 1933 item announced new steel towers, so the 1933 tower probably replaced an earlier one. The sources do not confirm when the 1933 tower was finished.
The register gives the lookout 7,590 ft. A trail guide gives 7,628 ft for the top of Towers Mountain. These may be different points on the summit.

notes_for_editor: Current access and staffing are unverified. 'In active service' comes from the 2003 register entry. I set access to restricted on that reading, so please check with the Bradshaw Ranger District. The Waymarking page did not render. Name variants: Tower Mountain (register, West Lookouts) and Towers Mountain (trail guide). The 1924 tower and 1933 tower are not clearly the same structure. No notable fires found in these sources.
